notes.title: 1.0 is live!
notes.content:
[p][b]After 2.5 years in Early Access, 6 years of total dev time, Plan B: Terraform has finally reached version 1.0![/b]

First of all, a huge thank you to our Early Access supporters. Your help during this period was invaluable. The game could not have become what it is today without your feedback, suggestions, and discussions. And a huge thanks to Crowdin contributors for helping with localization!
[/p][p]Most of the major changes were introduced in previous updates (so they could be tested and balanced with the help of our Early Access players – thank you so much!). But for this special milestone, we’ve kept a few surprises for today’s release:[/p][list][*][p][b]Controllable Animals[/b]: once oxygen is high enough, animals are released into the wild. You can now take direct control of them – including soaring as an eagle to admire your planet from a whole new perspective (with a free camera around the animal).[/p][/*][*][p][b]Creative Mode[/b]: new tools let you freely reshape your planet – add or remove water, mountains, minerals, and more. Options are also available for unlimited resources, fewer constraints, and total creative freedom. Access it anytime from the pause menu.[/p][/*][*][p][b]6 new music tracks[/b], for a total of 1h40 of immersive atmosphere in your terraformed worlds.[/p][/*][/list][p]Also, the sound design has been completely overhauled – the improvement is noticeable![/p][previewyoutube="YagJPANKF2Q;full"][/previewyoutube][p]Here’s a selection of the major improvements from previous updates. It’s been a long road, but absolutely worth it![/p][h3]
0.9.6: [/h3][list][*][p]Complete sound design overhaul[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Full localisation[/p][/*][/list][h3]0.9.5: [/h3][list][*][p]New terrain tool[/p][/*][/list][h3]0.9.4:[/h3][list][*][p]Grass everywhere (including under roads, rails, buildings)[/p][/*][*][p]More efficient drones & transports[/p][/*][*][p]Cities no longer require O₂ once enough oxygen[/p][/*][/list][h3]0.9.3:[/h3][list][*][p]Multi-selection and copy/paste[/p][/*][*][p]Undo/Redo[/p][/*][*][p]Visible ice on mountains & polar forests[/p][/*][/list][h3]0.9.1: [/h3][list][*][p]Drone performance upgrades[/p][/*][/list][h3]0.9 major update (2025-03-13):[/h3][list][*][p]All levels redesigned, now totaling 23, with new objectives and a newly added story told through dialogs.[/p][/*][*][p]New items: Space Elevator, Research Centers, Farms & Silos, Defense Fields[/p][/*][*][p]UI completely reworked: minimap, item bar, favorite system, item categories, oxygen visible in charts[/p][/*][*][p]Info panel, unlocked progressively (replacing both help and tutorial).[/p][/*][*][p]New achievements[/p][/*][/list][h3]0.8.3: [/h3][list][*][p]Automatic rail & road bridges[/p][/*][/list][h3]0.8.2: [/h3][list][*][p]Flying cars in cities, improved skybox[/p][/*][/list][h3]0.8 major update (2024-06-27):[/h3][list][*][p]Better world generation with large oceans & improved mountain shapes[/p][/*][*][p]New items: container ships, terrain modification tools, palm trees, cactus, tropical trees[/p][/*][*][p]Dynamic visible clouds[/p][/*][*][p]Improved enhanced view[/p][/*][*][p]Steam Workshop modding[/p][/*][*][p]New music tracks[/p][/*][/list][h3]0.7.5: [/h3][list][*][p]Performance improvements[/p][/*][*][p]New intermediary zoom level[/p][/*][/list][h3]0.7.3: [/h3][list][*][p]Warnings[/p][/*][/list][h3]0.7.2:[/h3][list][*][p]Drag & drop of items[/p][/*][/list][h3]0.7 major update (2023-11-06):[/h3][list][*][p]Achievements[/p][/*][*][p]New items: dam pumps, landmarks[/p][/*][*][p]Drone priority system, Backup Supply option[/p][/*][*][p]World generation options[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Game options[/p][/*][/list][p]
I would also like to thank again all the players of my previous game, [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/315460/Dig_or_Die"]Dig or Die[/url], as it is the success of that game that made [b]Plan B: Terraform[/b] possible. [/p][p]While I developed Dig or Die alone, Plan B was made by a (small) team. So, as a conclusion, I would like to sincerely thank my partners who were with me through most of the development: [b]Marion Santoni[/b] (who did all the art!) and [b]Romain Minguet[/b] (a fellow programmer always motivated — without him we would never have had multi-selection and many other features!).[/p][p]Thanks also to [b]Camille Gineste[/b] for her incredible soundtrack, and to [b]Léo Caillac[/b] for his last-minute heroic save on the sound design. And finally, [b]Aurélien Marck[/b] and [b]Guillaume Pivot[/b] for their help during the early steps of the game.[/p][p]Now... have a good game![/p][h3][/h3][p][/p][h3]Plan B - v1.0 build 1163 HOTFIX - 2025-08-30[/h3][p]- Fixed "crackling" sound in enhanced view on/off and factories and extractor looped sounds[/p][p]- Fixed Japanese texts in Info page[/p][p]- Fixed Korean broken info page[/p][p]- Fixed rare bug with hexagons belonging to two cities at the same time[/p][p]- Fixed some errors with minimap on very populated world (I mean alosapien's world of 5 billions pop)[/p][h3][/h3][h3]Plan B - v1.0 build 1166 HOTFIX - 2025-09-01[/h3][p]- Fixed memory leak when copying lot of items. notes.title: Plan B - v0.9.3: copy-paste!
notes.content:
The most suggested feature is here: select multiple unit with a selection box and copy-paste them anywhere with a Ctrl+C!
You can also undo and redo your previous action with (Shift+)Ctrl+Z.

Also, you now have ice on mountains tops and on forest grounds near poles.

Remark: For the selection, there might be some position offset when you copy or paste over pentagon/heptagons, but those are highlighted so you'll see if this is the case.

[h3]Plan B - v0.9.3 build 1014 [/h3]

[b]Major improvements:[/b][list]
[*] Multiple selection, copy (Ctrl+C), cut (Ctrl+X), paste (Ctrl+V). 
Use selection box, double click, and modifier shift/ctrl to add/remove from selection. 
Use E/R to mirror or rotate selection. 
Export or import selection to windows clipboard (Shift+C, Shift+V)
[*] Undo (Ctrl+Z) or redo (Shift+Ctrl+Z)
[/list]
[b]Improvements:[/b][list]
[*] Drag system improved (ghost item while dragged). Need some time to trigger, to differenciate from selection box
[*] Display ice on mountains and under forests in poles, and in high mountains in lower latitudes
[*] Add mouse wheel sensitivity option
[*] Dynamite mountain models more discreet
[*] add info page for selection, copy-paste, ctrl-build, undo
[/list]
[b]Bugs fix:[/b][list]
[*] Fixed bug with space that toggle menu
[*] Fixed ship path over spacelift cable
[*] Fixed ship path flashing in green/yellow
[*] Fixed water flow line going crazy after a terrain level tool
[*] Fixed bug with info panel
[/list]
[b]Minor:[/b][list]
[*] Update loc from/to Crowdin
[/list]

notes.title: Plan B - v0.9.2
notes.content:
Here is more than 50 improvements for the game! 
Nothing game-breaking, but we did a complete review and sorting of all the remaining tasks for the game, and we were able to complete a lot of old ones that had been reported/suggested a very long time ago! And now we know exactly what we have to do up to the v1.0 release (still planned for Q3 of this year).

And we are currently working on a very interesting and long awaited feature... So don't hesitate to join the discord and the Beta branch, to follow the development and help us by giving feedback on the new features!

notes.title: Plan B - v0.9 major update
notes.content:
v0.9 is the biggest update of the game, with new levels, new items, new mechanics, a story and a completely reworked UI!

The new content is pretty much everywhere, especially in the mid and late game. But above all, it completes the game as a whole, just as it was originally conceived. And the new content adds a link and coherence between the different elements: trees produce the oxygen that farms need, research centers lead to the expansion of secondary cities and link them together, and so on.

A few important things to note:

- [b]SAVE RESET[/b]: old saved games are not compatible with this new version. To continue playing old games, activate the branch "v0.8.4" (in the Steam properties of the game). I'm sorry for that, we didn't have choice, too many breaking changes in this update. But it's the only time it will happen, you'll be able to continue playing with v0.9 after v1.0 release.

- [b]MOD ERRORS[/b]: if the game cannot load, please check if you have some mods (steamworks or bepinex) as most of them are not yet compatible with v0.9

- [b]LOCALISATION / CROWDIN[/b] : if you wish to help translate a few sentences, you are most welcome! Here is the Crowdin page: https://crowdin.com/project/plan-b-terraform/invite/public


There will be a 20% discount during the Spring Sale, before the price is increased from $14 to $16 (the final price for the v1.0 release). It was the same with v0.7 and v0.8: the idea is that you pay only for what is already done, rather than for promises.

We will now be working on a number of small features, but above all on polishing and balancing. Then we will work on some small bonus for 1.0 (scheduled for release in Q3 of this year), like a nice creative mode.

notes.title: v0.9 progress
notes.content:
Here are some news about the v0.9 update, the biggest update of the game.

What is already done and can be played in the beta branch:
- A completely reworked UI, including an improved minimap that you can resize or hide, and a new Information panel (replacing the tutorial and the help - info pages will be unlocked progressively when there are new mechanics to learn).
- A dialog system, to brief the player before each levels, and progress along a simple storyline.
- Levels 1 to 11. No new game mechanics in those levels, but a lot of changes in the objectives, recipes, etc.
- And lot of various small fixes and improvements.

As i had explained before, it requires to start a new world, but it should be the only time. And you'll always be able to continue player v0.8x games if you wish (dedicated steam branch).

We are now working on the 2nd batch of levels, 12 to 18, which should come on the beta branch soon. Those will contain the space elevator you can see in the picture, along some related new game mechanics.
And then we'll work on the last levels, 19 to 25, with very exiting new mechanics too!

In addition to the sand graphic and other various improvements and bug fixes, two major bugs from the previous v0.8.3 have been fixed : the trucks loading too slowly, and the game freezing when building a rail end over a pentagon (in a specific direction). Very sorry for those bugs!

We are now going to focus on the v0.9, which will bring a lot of new content and a simple story. 
v0.9 will be incompatible with previous saves (starting with the next beta update), so I've created a "v0.8.4 backup" steam branch. This way you will always be able to continue to play with older games.

notes.title: Plan B - v0.8 major update
notes.content:
v0.8 is a major update for the planet's environment. Enjoy the new world generation with vast oceans and container ships to cross them. Open paths with the new dynamite and terrain tools. Get a better overview of your industry with a new zoom that show the atmospheric currents and cloud simulation, and an enhanced and unified view. Visualize ground humidity and choose between the five available trees, each with their own temperature and humidity requirements.
Five musics have also been added, and the original soundtrack will be available in a few days (for $5).

I suggest to start a new world to enjoy the new generation, but you can continue your old save. However, it will add a lot of water. If you wish to avoid such change, you can activate the "v0.7.5" beta (in the "beta" menu of the steam properties of the game) to keep playing the old version.
Edit: if you have installed a bepinex mod, you might have to remove it, as it could make the loading freeze.

The game will have a 20% discount during the Summer Sale, and then its price will increase from $12 to $14. It was the same with v0.7 and will be the same with v0.9: the idea is that you pay only for what is already done, rather than for promises.


Here is the full changelog:


[h3]Plan B - v0.8.0 build 879[/h3]

[b]Major Improvements:[/b][list]

notes.content:
Finally, the major performance increase upgrade is live! You might get x2 or better boost in framerate. 
It was a much bigger task than anticipated, but we took the time to explore every optimisation that we could think of. And it was definitely worth it, the result is much better than anticipated.

We also took the opportunity to add the long requested intermediary zoom (between the zoomed levels with all details and the planet-scale view).

notes.title: Team
notes.content:
After a few weeks of vacations, i'm now back to work on the v0.7 - to be released early October. Feel free to help test it by activating the beta branch, to test the depots priority system for example.

But for now, i wanted to take a few moment to introduce the people who worked with me on the game.

- Marion ([url=https://www.artstation.com/marion_santoni]artstation[/url]) did pretty much all the art for the game ! All 3D models come from her. 
I was able to hire her for two years, thanks to the success of my previous game Dig or Die, and a french aid fund (FAJV from CNC). 
When you've been a solo dev for years - unable to do make decent art yourself - working with someone who can make your vision of a game a reality, who can transform what you had in your head, into a real, living 3D world... it's such an incredible feeling!
And very good news, thanks to the success of Plan B Early Access, she's back this week for one more year! So she'll be able to add more models to the game, like more variations in the city, or the new items planned for the v0.9.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43157461/a10073a3c992cebffe716bc5c33c57c71e07d146.png[/img]

- Camille ([url=https://soundcloud.com/camillegineste]soundcloud[/url]) composed all the musics for the game. Game music is something incredibly important to me, and i'm very picky in the music choices and quality. So I think I was so lucky to be able to work with Camille. I instantly loved some of the musics she'd done before, and i knew it would fit very well with the game. And i'm so happy with the result - i hope you are too! The musics really adds something to the game.
And as for Marion, thanks to Plan B success, she has started working on additional musics for the 
game!

- Romain worked as an intern for a few months, helping me on the programming of the game. And teaching me modesty when taking some breaks on https://code.golf/ or https://www.codingame.com/ ;-)
And he too is back this week to work on the updates!


That's it for this little news. Thanks again for your support. The next news should be the V0.7 update, early october. notes.title: Why develop Plan B: Terraform?
notes.content:
Today, I would like to go back a bit to the origin of the game.

It all started with Factorio. What an incredible game (the best game in the world? or is it Subnautica? no, it's Outer Wilds of course)!
No subscreens everywhere, no transports complicated to set up (hello Transport Tycoon). Everything is visual, you can follow the resources from the beginning to the end... really great! But also so grey, so sad...

Add a bit of Mini Metro (for transports creation simplicity) and Cities Skyline (for its simple and efficient level structure), and you have the main inspirations for the game.

So, 4 years ago (and after working for 5 years on Dig or Die), I started this new game, Plan B: Terraform.

A "factorio but more pleasing to the eye, more chill" was only one aspect of what I wanted:

- After Dig or Die, I wanted to use my water cycle simulation engine again, but in a context that would perhaps make more sense: the terraformation of a planet. My interest was to have a progressive, slow terraformation, where influencing some parameters would naturally modify the world, relying only on the simulation. Just the opposite of an instant, artificial, "upgrade button" type of terraforming.

- I also wanted a very, very large terrain. Frustrated by some games where you build trains to connect cities that are 100 meters apart, I wanted to give an impression of gigantism, of vast landscapes to cross. An almost infinite playground, which would not be intended to be exploited to the maximum, but to convey this impression of gigantism, and the scale of the terraforming project.

- Finally, I wanted to insist on the "scale up" aspect of the population, of the industry. I wanted a game where the orders of magnitude at the end were really different from the start. 
This goes hand in hand with the two previous points, to give the player the impression of a real evolution during the game, of a complete change.

And thanks to the income from Dig or Die, and a help fund from the CNC in France, I was able to start this project serenely, being accompanied (among others) by a 3D artist during two years, and a composer. I'll come back to these talents in another blog post.

Thanks for reading, and sorry for my bad english. And ok, ok, now I go back to the updates!

Gaddy

It will also be much easier to handle the little changes on each game update. You can discuss in on the [url=https://discord.gg/gaddygames ]discord [/url](channel #translation-crowdin)

- We now have a [url=https://planbterraform.wiki.gg/wiki/Plan_B_Terraform_Wiki ][b]wiki[/b][/url]: 
It's still a very early state. I will (as soon as possible...) add items pages with data from the game, including all recipes. I created a #wiki channel on the [url=https://discord.gg/gaddygames]discord[/url] to discuss it.
